scope: gene-rule corrections for the four EMBL draft models, one per (organism, reaction). Each was adjudicated from the RefSeq product annotation of the genes in the rule and general enzymology only — never from the fitness data — under three written rules: (1) a gene whose product name denotes a different enzyme, a protein family or domain, or a non-enzymatic protein is removed from an OR rule; (2) genes annotated as subunits of one heteromeric enzyme are joined with AND; (3) paralogs carrying the same product name (plasmid copies, isozymes, promiscuous relatives) are left alone even where the fitness data suggest one is not functional, because annotation cannot tell them apart. The fitness benchmark then judges (scripts/evaluate_patch.py). Gene identifiers are Fitness Browser locus tags; they are translated to model gene ids when applied.

rules.R1: remove genes annotated as a different enzyme, a family/domain, or a non-enzymatic protein
rules.R2: join annotated subunits of one complex with AND
rules.R4: add an annotated isozyme that the draft omitted (gene present in the genome annotation, absent from the model)
